I've tried a build of v1.19.2 with this fix, but the `machine_` metrics become stale and disappear from Prometheus since they are now timestamped: https://github.com/google/cadvisor/commit/738f136b2badcaf86b3365a9d9c055aca5a45522 The kubelet only collects these metrics once and assumes a reboot for any updates. While cadvisor's manager will start a goroutine that updates them every 5min (configurable).

I'm not sure why the machine info metrics needed to be timestamped, but this seems to breaks how the kubelet cached them until now. Unless the Prometheus config disables `honor_timestamps` for this specific scrape job.

Thanks for pointing that out @basvdlei. It looks like that is run as part of the manager, still trying to grok why this code is different or how it relates to other cadvisor code in the kublet, like here: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/5d6dc8d19ce9209fa1e21e587996626f784ebc6a/pkg/kubelet/cadvisor/cadvisor_linux.go#L135

I was checking that has not been resolved in the 1.19.3 release. Due PR is not ready. So I had to stay with kubelet 1.18.9 and kubeadm and kubectl 1.19.3. Is there any better workaround for this? Or in this case running cadvisor as a separate ds?. I don't know if this last be a good practice.

A tricky fix is change cached machine info timestamp when get it:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/425fb7e4d301affa298397ef52d5d0eaf3d54a66/pkg/kubelet/kubelet_getters.go#L383-L388

To:

```go
// GetCachedMachineInfo assumes that the machine info can't change without a reboot
func (kl *Kubelet) GetCachedMachineInfo() (*cadvisorapiv1.MachineInfo, error) {
	kl.machineInfoLock.RLock()
	defer kl.machineInfoLock.RUnlock()
	clone := kl.machineInfo.Clone()
	clone.Timestamp = time.Now() //
	return clone, nil
}
```

@basvdlei Do you mind to try this PR with a fix in [this comment](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/95210#issuecomment-722994386) ? I haven't tested it yet, but I believe it should solve the problem you described.

Yes, it definitely is a temporary workaround, and I am not sure if it can be merged into k8s codebase.
I think the timestamp is a cadvisor design, maybe should open a issue in [its repo](https://github.com/google/cadvisor/issues).

I took a little bit more time to look into this. The collector will only include [a timestamp when it's non-zero](https://github.com/google/cadvisor/blob/65fa5b44d3840d465a5c004a0f6722e0fd540137/metrics/prometheus_machine.go#L240). So it's just a small fix to get the old behavior back, by setting the timestamp to zero before caching the machineInfo:

```diff
diff --git a/pkg/kubelet/kubelet.go b/pkg/kubelet/kubelet.go
index 2fdd321e583..7ccb28daad2 100644
--- a/pkg/kubelet/kubelet.go
+++ b/pkg/kubelet/kubelet.go
@@ -561,6 +561,7 @@ func NewMainKubelet(kubeCfg *kubeletconfiginternal.KubeletConfiguration,
        if err != nil {
                return nil, err
        }
+       machineInfo.Timestamp = time.Time{}
        klet.setCachedMachineInfo(machineInfo)
 
        imageBackOff := flowcontrol.NewBackOff(backOffPeriod, MaxContainerBackOff)
```

issue_context.title: Missing cadvisor machine metrics (v1.19)
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


**What happened**:
prometheus cadvisor machine metrics from kubelet are missing
```
# kubectl get --raw "/api/v1/nodes/NODE_NAME/proxy/metrics/cadvisor" | grep -i machine_cpu_cores
```

**What you expected to happen**:
```
# kubectl get --raw "/api/v1/nodes/NODE_NAME/proxy/metrics/cadvisor" | grep -i machine_cpu_cores
# HELP machine_cpu_cores Number of CPU cores on the machine.
# TYPE machine_cpu_cores gauge
machine_cpu_cores 4
```

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
install k8s 1.19, compare behavior to k8s <1.19

**Anything else we need to know?**:
Looks like missing call to `NewPrometheusMachineCollector` in `pkg/kubelet/server/server.go`, machine metrics collection was split out in cadvisor 0.37

**Environment**:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`):
```
Client Version: version.Info{Major:"1", Minor:"19", GitVersion:"v1.19.2+k3s1", GitCommit:"d38505b124c92bffd45f6e0654adb9371cae9610", GitTreeState:"clean", BuildDate:"2020-09-29T20:53:06Z", GoVersion:"go1.15.1", Compiler:"gc", Platform:"linux/amd64"}
Server Version: version.Info{Major:"1", Minor:"19", GitVersion:"v1.19.2+k3s1", GitCommit:"d38505b124c92bffd45f6e0654adb9371cae9610", GitTreeState:"clean", BuildDate:"2020-09-29T20:53:06Z", GoVersion:"go1.15.1", Compiler:"gc", Platform:"linux/amd64"}
```
comments: Suggest `kube_node_status_capacity{resource="cpu"}` from [kube-state-metrics](https://github.com/kubernetes/kube-state-metrics/blob/master/docs/node-metrics.md) as an alternative (declared as "stable").

Related PR https://github.com/google/cadvisor/pull/2444

Their output format changed too:
```
machine_cpu_cores{boot_id="f458180f-6fca-45e7-9e6f-b4cadae32e1a",machine_id="0dd757ddac4841a7a5873e054f810738",system_uuid="0dd757dd-ac48-41a7-a587-3e054f810738"} 2 1604654611200
```
Multiple queries is invalide now. Is there any workaroud for this? Please help. Thanks.
@dongwangdw if you run `kube-state-metrics` see https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/95204#issuecomment-719445180 for an alternative metric.
+1 on the issue. This issue has caused the node metric collection for Azure Monitor for Containers to be broken which also impacts alerting.
Exposed metrics are a kind of an API and should not be removed without warning.

any news, when this will be fixed?
Thanks in advance!

> Exposed metrics are a kind of an API and should not be removed without warning.

It is not possible to have a metric available without exposing it. To provide stability information on metrics, similar to APIs, you might want to read up on the [Kubernetes metric stability framework](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/blob/master/keps/sig-instrumentation/20190404-kubernetes-control-plane-metrics-stability.md). There currently are no metrics in Kubernetes itself that are considered stable, but SIG Instrumentation hopes to be selecting some for the 1.21 release.

This particular issue seems like an unintended bug as opposed to an intentional deprecation.

Suspect this issue got lost in SIG Node's backlog. I'll put it on the agenda for the next SIG Instrumentation meeting.


/sig instrumentation
